items.headline: AI companies are buying hardcover books and destroying them
items.excerpt: AI firms are sourcing physical books through commercial channels and pulping them after scanning. The fear for preservationists is that rare titles that can never be replaced are being destroyed for training data.

items.headline: FTC asked to investigate destruction of books
items.excerpt: More than a dozen groups have asked the Federal Trade Commission to look at the scanning and destruction of physical books for AI model training.

items.headline: Anthropic Adds Watermarks to Claude's AI-Generated Text
items.excerpt: Anthropic is adding watermarks to text generated by Claude, raising new questions about AI transparency, provenance and disclosure for AI-assisted books.

items.headline: How Claude watermarking works: Some accuse Anthropic of compliance theatre
items.excerpt: Commentators find it problematic that the watermark is applied when Claude is used for assistive tasks rather than purely generative ones — a distinction that matters for writers who use AI to edit.

items.headline: Amazon is buying and scanning books to train AI
items.excerpt: A sober read on the Amazon VGT3 scanning story: breathless coverage misses that many of the destroyed books may be out of date and commercially undesirable.

items.headline: These are all of the new Spotify audiobook features
items.excerpt: A rundown of Spotify's recent audiobook push, including AI-assisted discovery such as prompt-built audiobook playlists and improved series tracking.

items.title: AI-generated books are flooding Amazon and tanking sales for human authors
items.excerpt: A new market study of the Amazon/Kindle catalog finds AI-assisted titles diluting the whole market: between Q1 2023 and Q1 2026 the catalog grew 38.3x while quarterly revenue grew only 8.9x. Books with no detected AI text are 62.9% of the catalog but 72.5% of revenue, while substantially-AI books are 20% of titles and 11.3% of revenue.
items.off_list_reason: Distinct from the already-published Originality.AI religion-paperback study; no on-list outlet carried this catalog-wide revenue-dilution analysis in the window.

items.title: 읽던 웹툰이 말을 걸었다…'보는 만화' 틀 깬 네이버웹툰
items.excerpt: 네이버웹툰이 원작자 승인 IP를 기반으로 독자가 웹툰 주인공과 직접 대화하는 AI 스토리챗 '바이어스(byUs)'와 AI 숏폼 제작 서비스 '컷츠메이크'를 전개하며 웹툰 소비 방식 자체를 바꾸고 있다. 휴재 중이던 '이직로그'는 AI 서비스 적용 후 일주일 만에 조회수가 67% 증가했다.
items.off_list_reason: Korean webtoon/comics publishing AI; no on-list domain covers Korean publishing.

items.title: Book Marketing, AI Book Discoverability, And Resilience, With Ricardo Fayet
items.excerpt: Reedsy co-founder Ricardo Fayet argues that AI search engines surface and recommend books on completely different signals than Amazon keyword search, so keyword SEO is giving way to 'generative engine optimization'. Authors are told to build an internet footprint — reviews, Goodreads, Reddit mentions — that chatbots can actually cite.

items.title: When bots write books
items.excerpt: A survey of how generative AI is being folded into book production — from drafting to the flood of machine-written titles reaching retail — and what that shift means for human authors, editors and the shape of the publishing pipeline.
items.off_list_reason: General-interest outlet, but a books-craft/industry piece; on-list literary outlets (Lit Hub, Book Riot, Electric Literature) had no fresh AI item in the window.

items.title: What Technology Trends Should Publishers Explore and Scale?
items.excerpt: Digital Publishing Report and Publishing Signal are launching an annual Publishing Technology Radar to tell publishers which technologies — AI tooling among them — are worth investing in, experimenting with, or waiting out. The global survey feeding it is open until August 30.
